sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Accounts Receivable Factoring and Cross-Border Reverse Factoring

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law with strong commercial law codification and Common Law influences in maritime and financial sectors
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama-United Kingdom Bilateral Investment Treaty and Double Taxation Agreement (limited scope)
Panama-Canada Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA)
Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards (New York Convention)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (as amended by Ley 254 de 2021 and Decreto Ejecutivo 202 de 2021), implementing FATF standards; UBO registry obligations under Resolución No. 093-2022 of the Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros; due diligence standards under Acuerdo No. 019-2021 of the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá; mandatory UBO filing to the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales maintained by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), per Ley 70 de 2019 and Decreto Ejecutivo 433 de 2021.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificado de Registro de la Sociedad)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the Panama Canal Area / Registro Público de Panamá

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (Pacto Social) and Bylaws (Estatutos)
Certificate of UBO Registration (Constancia de Inscripción del Beneficiario Final)
Identity and Good Standing Certificate for Directors, Officers and Shareholders (Certificado de Antecedentes Penales and DPI copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Tribunal Electoral de Panamá (DPI) / Procuraduría General de la Nación (criminal background)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all prospective shareholders, directors, officers, and ultimate beneficial owners against UN Security Council consolidated lists, OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UK OFSI consolidated list, and Panama's national terrorism financing list (Listado de Personas Vinculadas a Financiamiento del Terrorismo). Enhanced due diligence required for any PEP, PEP family members, or close associates; beneficial owners must provide verified source of funds and source of wealth declarations. The relationship must be reported to the compliance officer of the legal service provider under Ley 23 de 2015 and the firm's internal AML/CFT manual.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá (Panama Public Registry) online portal: www.registropublico.gob.pa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names may be registered in Spanish, English, or any other Latin-script language. All names must include a corporate identifier token such as 'S.A.', 'Corp.', 'Inc.', or 'Sociedad Anónima'. If the name is provided in a non-Latin script, an official transliteration into the Latin alphabet must be submitted; for Cyrillic or Asian characters, a certified linguist transliteration is required. The name must be distinctive and not misleading as to the corporate purpose.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant may request a second pre-clearance search or file a written appellate request (Recurso de Apelación) with the Dirección General de Registros del Registro Público within 10 business days of the rejection notice. The appeal must include a memorial identifying the proposed name, the rejecting official, the grounds of rejection, and a legal argument demonstrating trademark availability and compliance with Article 20 of the Panama Companies Law (Ley 32 de 1927). A negative name clearance certificate may be reissued after adjusting the name and re-submitting the application through the authorized notary or registered agent. If the appeal is denied at the initial level, the applicant may file a second administrative reconsideration (Recurso de Reconsideración) before the Registro General within 5 additional business days; final denial triggers a civil law action before the Juzgado Tercero Civil del Primer Circuito Judicial de Panamá.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not considered a valid registered office for an active factoring corporation. The Sociedad Anónima must maintain a physical registered office in Panama and a resident agent (agente residente) who must be an attorney or law firm licensed in Panama. The factoring activity requires operative substance, including a local establishment, real management, and physical records. For enhanced AML/CFT compliance, the Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros and the DGI may require a physical address for accounting records, invoice registers, and UBO files; the exclusive use of a virtual office triggers economic substance risk under the OECD tax transparency framework and may lead to the application of Panama's economic substance requirements under Decreto Ejecutivo 299 de 2019.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (estimated 85% for licensed factoring entities due to the medium-risk AML classification, mandatory sector supervision by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá, and regular anti-money laundering on-site visits; probability increases in the first five years for factoring and supply-chain finance entities because of the 2021 amendments to Ley 23 strengthening preventive supervision; inspection campaigns are supported by on-site presence of the Unidad de Análisis Financiero).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial fee for the public deed and notarization of the articles of incorporation (Pacto Social) and signature authenticities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary Public of the Panama Canal Area / Fourth Commercial Notary of Panama
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official notary tariff schedule (Arancel Notarial) and prevailing market tariff for full incorporation bundle

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration fees at the Panama Public Registry (Registro Público de Panamá) for corporate registration, including provisional name registration and filing of the incorporation documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff per Registro Público fee schedule for 2024 (Decree 393 and unified tariff official schedule)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO initial registration fee (primer registro de beneficiario final) at the Dirección General de Ingresos
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed tribunal fee per DGI Tax Code (Código Fiscal, Article 719-A) and Executive Decree 433 of 2021

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Resident agent service fee for one year, including registered office, mail forwarding and compliance coordination
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed resident agent (abogado autorizado) in Panama
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for corporate legal services in Panama City (typical range: USD 300–500)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and preliminary search and certificate issuance (Certificado de Búsqueda onomástica)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Standard statutory fee for name search and written certificate; includes in-person and online search fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille fees for the notarized incorporation bundle (Certificate of Incorporation and UBO certificate), per document
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Panama (apostille office)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Uniform consular and apostille fee schedule set by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (approximately USD 10 per document x2 documents; budget lumped with processing)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: License application for factoring and supply-chain finance operation under the Special Regime for Financial Support Companies (Ley 82 de 2019)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros (SSN) / Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (industry-specific)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory authorization and annual fee for non-bank financial support entities, as published in official fee schedules; actual license amount may vary from USD 1,000 to USD 1,500 for medium-risk factoring platform

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Attorney professional fee for full pre-incorporation due diligence, legalization, name clearance and UBO piercing file preparation (flat fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panama City law firm (external corporate counsel)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing professional fee for corporate formations with factoring license and enhanced AML/CFT components (market benchmark for mid-market boutique law firms)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT customer due diligence file setup and compliance officer initial designation (including internal KYC software or file registry)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance officer of the licensed Panama law firm and the entity's designated AML/CFT officer
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Standard compliance administration fee included in the legal services retainer; reflects the cost of electronic KYC verification, PEP database subscription and record keeping upgrades

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Economic substance notification and OECD Common Reporting Standard indicator registration (optional preliminary filing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: DGI administrative filing fee for tax and economic substance forms (Registro de Información Fiscal)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Panama General Law of Corporations (Ley General de Sociedades), enacted by Law 32 of 1927, as amended; key sections include Article 2 (contents of public instrument), Article 5 (registered office requirement), Article 10 (purposes), Article 58 (issuance of shares), and Article 62 (directors and officers).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá), Mercantile Section – Panama City
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public Deed of Incorporation (Escritura Pública de Constitución) or officiated Certificate of Incorporation for S.A. entities
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital requirement under Panamanian law; the company must issue at least one share of any nominal value. Paid-up capital may be nominal or zero, and no escrow account is required for incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME], S.A. The undersigned directors, constituting a quorum, unanimously resolve: (1) the company hereby subscribes or approves the subscription of shares as set forth in the register of shareholders; (2) the registered office is fixed at the address provided to the Public Registry of Panama; (3) the following individuals are appointed to hold office with full authority: President, Secretary, Treasurer, and Resident Agent in accordance with the bylaws; (4) the appointed officers are authorized to execute banking documents, negotiate credit facilities, and establish an escrow account for trade finance operations; (5) all prior actions of incorporators are ratified; and (6) this resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama, Mercantile Section – online name reservation system (OPC – Ventanilla Electrónica)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request through the Public Registry's electronic platform or in person. The requester must provide up to three proposed names, each ending with 'S.A.' The Registrar checks for conflicts with existing registered names. If available, the name is reserved for a statutory period, usually 30 days, during which the public deed must be submitted for registration.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation application form
Identification document (passport or corporate ID) of the applicant
Power of attorney, if filed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity, the applicant may file a written administrative reconsideration with the Mercantile Section, or submit alternative names immediately. No material adverse consequence if corrected within the reservation window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama (Notaría Pública)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: A Panamanian attorney drafts the corporation bylaws and articles of incorporation, including the corporate purpose covering accounts receivable factoring, reverse factoring, and trade supply chain financing. The draft is presented to a notary for execution by the incorporators. The notary authenticates the signatures and issues the 'Protocolización' (notarization) before the original Escritura Pública is sent to the Public Registry.
required_dossiers: Certificate of name reservation from the Public Registry
Draft incorporation bylaws (Pacto Social y Estatutos)
Identification documents of incorporators and initial directors
Written consent of nominated Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a legal defect or missing signature, the incorporators are contacted to execute corrective documents or addenda. Resubmission for notarization is possible without loss of the name reservation if completed within the reservation term.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Public Deed with the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama, Mercantile Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notarized Public Deed of Incorporation is physically or electronically submitted to the Public Registry for inscription. The Registry verifies the name, legal form, capital structure, registered office, resident agent, and directors. Upon successful review, the corporation is granted a legal personality evidenced by the Inscripción (registration) of the company number. The registration fee is paid at authorized bank branches or electronic payment points.
required_dossiers: Original notarized Escritura Pública de Constitución
Two certified copies of the public deed
Receipt of payment of registration fees
Original name reservation certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues an 'observación' or rejection notice, counsel may file a prompt correction and resubmission within the legally applicable response period. In the event of substantive issues, a new public deed amendment is executed and re-presented for registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Identification Registration and Municipal Operating License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Directorate of Revenue (Dirección General de Ingresos – DGI) and Municipality of Panama (Alcaldía de Panamá)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the company is registered with the Public Registry, the legal representative must obtain the Número de RUC (tax identification number) from the DGI. The company must also apply for a municipal operating license (Aviso de Operación) with the relevant municipality, declaring the business activity under the Código Industrial Internacional Uniforme (CIIU) corresponding to financial services, and obtain the official municipal registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation issued by the Public Registry
Completed tax registration form (Formulario de Registro Único de Contribuyentes)
Copy of the identification card or passport of the legal representative
Municipal application form for Aviso de Operación
Proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI or municipality identifies a documentation gap, the applicant may file a corrective amendment with the competent authority within ten business days. Missing field indexes may be remedied through an online correction portal or by submitting a revised sworn statement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Antr Trust / Compliance Vetting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank (licensed by the Superintendency of Banks of Panama) and Anti-Money Laundering Compliance Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The appointed officers open a corporate bank account, typically requiring the certified articles of incorporation, RUC certificate, municipal permit, and two sworn references. The bank will conduct know-your-client (KYC) and due diligence checks, and for a factoring company, an enhanced due diligence (EDD) process applies because of the financial nature of the business. The account is opened for escrow and wire transfer payment rails.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Public Registry inscription
Copy of RUC and municipal aviso de operación
Minutes of the First Board Resolution appointing signatories
Certified passports and proof of address of directors and beneficial owners
Bank-provided KYC/EDD questionnaire
Reference letters from professional firms or commercial banks
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further information, the company may provide additional source-of-funds declarations and background information. If the account opening is delayed beyond statutory clarity, the company may submit to any commercial bank complaint channel or apply to a different licensed bank in Panama; no statutory adverse action arises from venue selection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce and Industries (Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias – MICI), General Directorate of Industries
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia Comercial / Industrial de Factoring y Financiamiento de Cadenas de Suministro (Commercial/Industrial License for Factoring and Supply Chain Financing)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (Ministerio de Ambiente – MiAMBIENTE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II – Registration and Moderate Impact Assessment, according to the Environmental Impact Assessment Regulations of Panama (Executive Decree 123 of 2014) – not a full EIA because the activity is office-based and does not involve major industrial infrastructure
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Panama's national wastewater discharge limits under Executive Decree No. 58 of 2003 for incidental sanitary wastewater; zero industrial process wastewater or VOC emissions are expected; any liquid waste from purged HVAC or cooling systems must meet the domestic sewage standard (temperature, pH 6-9, BOD5 < 250 mg/L, total suspended solids < 300 mg/L). If the registered office is in a mixed-use building, the building operator's environmental clearance may apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Panama Fire Department (Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá), a structural load inspection certificate from a licensed Panamanian civil engineer, and an occupational workplace clearance from the Ministry of Labor and Labor Development (MITRADEL) are required. For a dedicated office used for financial operations, fire extinguishers, emergency exits, and basic workplace safety signage must be installed and certified before the municipality issues final operation approval.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); online services via Sede Electrónica DGI (https://dgi.gob.pa).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Panama Sociedad Anónima: (1) notarize the incorporation deed (Escritura Pública) and register it with the Registro Público de Panamá to obtain the corporate Folio; (2) appoint a resident registered agent (abogado idóneo) and maintain a local registered office; (3) obtain the municipal Aviso de Operación from the relevant Municipality; (4) file the RUC registration (Formulario RUC) with DGI through the Sede Electrónica, attaching the certified deed, Public Registry certificate, registered-agent authorization, municipal aviso, and identification of directors/shareholders, obtaining the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) normally within 5–10 business days; (5) register the taxable activity, including ITBMS activity and required withholding-agent status; (6) obtain the electronic invoicing authorization where applicable; and (7) open a Panamanian bank account to evidence inward remittances. Non-resident ownership is permitted, and no minimum paid-in capital is required for a standard S.A.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide check-the-box or pass-through elections for S.A.s; the S.A. is a per se corporation taxed at entity level only on Panama-source income under the territorial system. Available statutory elections include: (i) the simplified small-taxpayer regime under Law 83/2015 (Régimen Especial Simplificado) where annual gross revenue is below the DGI-published cap; (ii) special elective regimes such as Multinational Headquarters (SEM, Law 41/2007), Colon Free Zone, Panapass, and City of Knowledge; (iii) election to allocate/prorate common expenses between taxable Panama-source income and exempt foreign-source income; and (iv) election to issue zero-rated electronic invoices with DGI hash/QR stamping for documented export transactions. Hybrid mismatch elections are not recognized; Panama has not enacted BEPS Action 2 hybrid mismatch rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) – Panama's VAT/GST-equivalent consumption tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold applies: every person engaged in taxable transfers of goods, taxable services, or imports must register for ITBMS (RUC-linked) before commencing operations. A reduced-compliance track (Régimen Especial Simplificado, Law 83/2015) is available for qualifying small taxpayers below the statutory annual gross-receipts cap published by DGI, but exporters, financial entities, and factoring companies must always obtain full ITBMS registration in order to issue zero-rated/exempt invoices and preserve input-credit or refund claims.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica de Panamá) is phased in by DGI according to annual-revenue segments. Taxpayers must use DGI-authorized billing software or the DGI Sede Electrónica and transmit invoices as structured XML via REST/API web services; each invoice receives a DGI sequential authorization number, digital hash, and QR-code stamp. Series subject to pre-clearance (validación previa) are validated before issuance. The electronic Comprobante de Crédito Fiscal (fiscal credit voucher) is required to support input ITBMS credits. Financial services and factoring discount/financing income must be coded with the applicable exempt or 0% rate, and underlying export documentation must be retained for DGI inspection.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports qualify for 0% ITBMS where the goods physically leave Panama under a valid Aduana export declaration within the prescribed customs time window. Services, including factoring and trade-finance services, qualify for 0% (or are statutorily exempt as pure financial services) where the recipient is a non-resident and the service is effectively consumed, used, or exploited outside Panama; the factoring/discount interest margin is exempt as a financial service, while fee-based commission components may be zero-rated where the foreign use/destination test is satisfied. The claimant must be a fully registered ITBMS taxpayer, issue 0%-rated electronic invoices, and retain documentary proof of physical export or offshore enjoyment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) with Aduana validation stamp
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical exit of goods
Inward Remittance Certificate – bank statement or SWIFT MT103 evidencing receipt of export/factoring proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI cross-matches zero-rating claims against customs declarations, electronic invoice data, and bank inward-remittance records. Unjustified 0% treatment is reversed retrospectively with the ITBMS assessed at 7% on the taxable amount, plus statutory monthly surcharge, interest, and fines up to 100% of the evaded tax for fraudulent misstatements. Improperly obtained refunds are clawed back with penalties, the exporter registration may be suspended, and criminal tax/customs fraud liability may be pursued under the Código Penal. The general assessment and clawback limitation period is five years, extended in cases of fraud or omitted registration.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No domestic central bank exists; the de facto monetary authority is the U.S. Federal Reserve under Panama's full dollarization regime. Financial, non-bank, and factoring activity is prudentially supervised by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP). There is no dedicated foreign exchange administration, and exchange policy is not separately regulated.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full currency convertibility prevails for both current and capital account transactions. No exchange controls, multiple exchange rates, surrender quotas, or advance approval mechanisms apply. Profit remittances, dividend distributions, and capital repatriations are unrestricted, subject only to Panamanian corporate formalities and territorial-tax compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama does not impose statutory timelines, mandatory surrender percentages, or conversion obligations for export receipts. Exporters and trade financiers may freely hold, convert, or remit foreign currency through SBP-licensed banks.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility as a primary clearing rail. Panama does not maintain a distinct electronic money institution (EMI) licence; non-bank payment service providers require SBP authorization under Acuerdo 3-2018 (payment system regulation) or must act as agents of licensed banks. Offshore digital EMIs without a Panamanian branch cannot settle domestic escrow obligations and will not be accepted as proof of banking infrastructure for factoring-license renewal or client money safeguarding.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Panamanian Sociedad Anónima engaged in factoring, directors and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) must generally appear physically before a notary public and, in most Tier-1 banks, complete an in-person compliance interview. Remote opening is exceptionally accepted for a non-resident shareholder only after initial physical onboarding of at least one director; a sworn power-of-attorney may then be used for transactional administration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered-agent shell structure and historical bearer-share exposure for the Panamanian corporation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the public deed of incorporation, duly maintained and notarized share register (Registro de Acciones), updated UBO declaration naming all natural-person shareholders, Panama tax registry (RUC) certificate, evidence of commercial substance (office lease, payroll, local bank statements), and an AML manual if the company is licensed as a factoring entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border factoring transactions involving multiple debtors, third-party payments, or invoice assignment without clear chain of ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed and notarized factoring agreements, underlying commercial invoices with delivery evidence (invoices, bills of lading, POD certificates), debtor credit-underwriting files, source-of-funds documentation, Correspondent Banking Questionnaires, and a transaction-flow map showing every assignment and payment leg.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlicensed provision of factoring services triggering SBP regulatory scrutiny
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of SBP factoring company licence or the official application track record, statutory financial statements, AML/CFT policies and procedures, appointment letter for the AML compliance officer, and registrations with the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) where applicable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inward capital injections must be routed through SWIFT MT103 in USD to the entity's operating or escrow account maintained at a SBP-licensed Panamanian bank. The receiving bank will require a sworn declaration (Declaración Jurada) identifying the sender, ultimate originator, beneficiary, and economic purpose code. For factoring receivables, the bank also requires delivery of the invoice assignment notice and the underlying trade contract to distinguish trade remittances from equity injections. Third-party personal accounts are prohibited as collection points for client funds or capital contributions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements to foreign suppliers, factored debtors, or assignor clients are executed via SWIFT MT103 (single customer transfers) or MT202 (bank-to-bank aggregation). Commercial Letters of Credit are issued through a Panamanian bank via SWIFT MT700 or confirmed/negotiated by international correspondent banks. Domestic payments may use Panama's local ACH system; cross-border liquidity is cleared through the U.S. correspondent network (usually CITI, BNY, or JP Morgan) given Panama's dollarized system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Short-dated and forward FX contracts through international bank counterparties for non-USD receivables (e.g., EUR, CNY, JPY) to lock in USD-equivalent factoring proceeds
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing emerging-market currencies against USD to hedge non-liquid currency exposure without physical settlement
Plain-vanilla cross-currency swaps under ISDA/CSA with licensed international banks, subject to board-approved treasury, netting, and credit-risk policies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Declaración de Rentas / Informe Anual de Sociedades)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Registro Público de Panamá (for franchise tax annual report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual Return (income tax): within 3 months following the fiscal year end (March 31 for calendar-year taxpayers). Annual franchise tax report: due by June 30 each year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 10% of the tax due, plus 1% per month of interest; continued non-compliance leads to administrative dissolution and strike-off after two consecutive years of unpaid franchise tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Franchise Tax Payment (Impuesto de Tasa Única)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (through licensed resident agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by January 15 for the preceding year; if the company's anniversary date is used, deadline is the last working day of the anniversary month.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment attracts a fine of USD 300 plus interest; after two years of non-payment, the company is struck off and the registered agent must file for reinstatement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Report and Board Resolution for Registered Agent Records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent / Registered Office Provider (retained for inspection by the Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the annual shareholders' meeting or by the anniversary date of incorporation, whichever is earlier.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain current records triggers registered agent resignation, loss of registered address, and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Transfer Pricing and Related-Party Transaction Documentation (if applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the income tax return (March 31 for calendar-year taxpayers); supporting documentation must be ready by the return date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties up to 1% of the value of related-party transactions, minimum USD 10,000; interest accrues from the due date.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Panama Companies Law (Law 32 of 1927 as amended) does not impose a universal statutory audit. Mandatory audit applies if the company is a regulated financial entity, if it is a public-interest entity, or if its annual gross revenue exceeds USD 3,000,000 or total assets exceed USD 3,000,000 as per DGI regulations. Factoring companies licensed under the Superintendencia de Bancos are audited annually regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB for licensed financial and factoring entities; local GAAP (NIIF/P.C.G.A. Panama) permitted for non-licensed commercial companies not exceeding mandatory audit thresholds.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Executive Decree 363 of 2015 and the Beneficial Ownership Law (Law 23 of 2015), companies must file an annual confidential UBO report by the anniversary of incorporation. Any transfer of 10% or more of shares must be reflected in the register within 30 days and the annual confirmation must be updated by the registered agent. Non-compliance carries fines up to USD 50,000.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Beneficial Ownership Record (Registro de Beneficiario Final)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 – USD 15,000 for a licensed factoring company, depending on transaction volume and cross-border portfolio complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama applies a territorial corporate income tax (ISR) at 25% on Panamanian-source profits. Foreign-source income is not taxed in Panama, provided it is separately accounted for and not attributable to a Panama permanent establishment. There is no general statutory tax holiday for factoring companies; preferential 5% ISR applies only to qualifying Multinational Headquarters (SEM) license holders. Deductions are limited to expenses direct and necessary for generating Panamanian-source income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 280 (Declaración de Renta para Personas Jurídicas) filed through the DGI Sede Electrónica portal at sede.dgi.gob.pa.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; advance ISR instalments are paid during the fiscal year, but Form 280 is the single final corporate income tax return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three calendar months after the fiscal-year end. For a calendar-year company, the deadline is 31 March of the following year. If the deadline falls on a non-business day, the due date shifts to the next business day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: RUC, corporate name, and fiscal-period dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Panama Sociedad Anónima files as a Panamanian-incorporated resident taxpayer even when all shareholders are non-resident. No foreign ownership data is entered in Form 280.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from Panamanian-source activities: factoring discounts, commissions, underwriting fees, guarantee fees, late-payment interest, and recovered receivable profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only revenue where the account-debtor, collateral, or payment risk is in Panama. Cross-border reverse factoring on foreign buyers is foreign-source revenue and must be disclosed separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source gross revenue accurately segregated from Panamanian-source revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source revenue is not subject to the 25% ISR but must be separately reported and supported by board resolutions, contracts, and invoices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible costs and expenses: funding cost, provisions for bad debts, operating rent, salaries, depreciation, and transfer-pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenses allocable to Panamanian-source revenue. Blanket head-office cost allocations from foreign affiliates are not deductible unless substantiated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income: Panamanian-source gross revenue less deductible expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute this line before set-off of prior-year losses; loss carryforward is limited to five years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: ISR computed at 25% on taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not file a separate Panama income tax return; the S.A. pays corporate ISR and then applies dividend withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepayments, withholding tax credits, and any applicable statutory credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Panama generally gives no foreign-tax credit for excluded foreign-source income. Use only DGI-recognised Panamanian-source prepayment credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a default surcharge on unpaid ISR, monthly statutory interest, administrative fines (typically B/.50 to B/.5,000 depending on delay), and denial of tax compliance certificates. Persistent non-filing may result in tax execution, judicial attachment, and criminal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withheld on dividends distributed from net profits subject to Panamanian corporate income tax; distributions from properly segregated foreign-source profits are not subject to Panama dividend tax. Bearer-share distributions may attract additional retention until bearer shares are exchanged and immobilised.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama applies a territorial system and has a compact network of comprehensive DTAs. To invoke a DTA at source, the non-resident beneficial owner must obtain a tax-residence certificate (TRC) from the treaty jurisdiction, file an exoneración application with the DGI, and submit proof of beneficial ownership, substantial economic activity, and the transaction chain. Reduced treaty rates are not self-executing; DGI confirmation is required before distribution or remittance. A Panamanian company claiming treaty benefits abroad must obtain a Panamanian TRC from the DGI.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Panamanian-source interest and royalty payments to non-residents are generally subject to a 12.5% final withholding advance against ISR, unless the income is demonstrably foreign-source. Under applicable comprehensive DTAs, treaty rates can reduce interest and royalty withholding to 5% or 0%, subject to TRC and beneficial-ownership conditions. Factoring discount paid by a Panamanian debtor to a non-resident financier is treated as Panamanian-source interest unless the credit is clearly supplied from abroad and does not create Panamanian situs.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: PAB 2,000,000 (USD 2,000,000, Balboa peg) in aggregate annual related-party transactions. Above this threshold, the taxpayer must prepare Local File, Master File, benchmarking analysis, and file the annual transfer-pricing annex with the DGI.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not apply Caribbean-format Economic Substance Regulations to ordinary S.A.s. However, DGI and AML authorities apply substance-over-form and a general anti-abuse rule. SEM-licensed factoring or finance companies must maintain physical presence, local employees, and substantive revenue activities. Shell companies using treaty benefits or interposing without business purpose are exposed to recalculation, denial of treaty rates, and corporate registry sanctions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omission of Panamanian-source factoring income, fabricated invoices, false bad-debt provisions, or use of unreported escrow wallets or SWIFT wiring to collect invoice settlements without declaring them.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI assessment of the full evaded ISR, statutory interest, administrative fines up to 100% of evaded tax, and criminal prosecution for tax fraud carrying 2 to 5 years imprisonment under the Panama Fiscal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or cause false declarations are jointly and severally liable for evaded taxes, interest, and fines. Serious cases trigger travel bans, asset attachments, and imprisonment of the responsible officers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Nominee-only governance, no Panamanian management, financial records kept abroad, bearer shares not immobilised, and no physical or economic activity while claiming tax or banking legitimacy.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Registry cancellation of corporate rights, administrative fines up to B/.100,000, adverse DGI anti-abuse determination, denial of treaty benefits, and filing as a reportable entity to FATF-style networks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced when the company is a mere alter ego. Directors become personally liable to creditors and tax authorities, face disqualification from Panamanian corporate directorship, and may be named in AML sanctions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Factoring transactions with related parties priced above or below arm's-length discount rates, understated default-risk fees, unjustified cost contributions, or profit-shifting to zero-tax jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary TP adjustment to arm's-length income, secondary adjustment treating the shortfall as a deemed distribution, penalties of 20% to 40% of the underpaid tax, and statutory interest. Documentation failure triggers additional fixed penalties determined by the DGI.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving non-arm's-length pricing or signing false TP documentation may be held personally liable for intentional mispricing and face monetary fines and disqualification from corporate office.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Holding out to Panamanian SMEs as a commercial factor or lender without the required license, using unauthorised third-party payment aggregators, failing to perform customer due diligence, or laundering proceeds through escrow accounts and SWIFT wires.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Panama's banking and AML laws, especially AML Law 23 of 2015, impose fines up to B/.1,000,000 per violation, suspension or revocation of any license, and criminal sentences of 5 to 12 years for money-laundering offences involving invoice trading.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Compliance officers and directors at fault face personal criminal indictment, freezing orders, travel bans, exclusion from financial-system management, and civil liability for fraud when the corporate form is abused.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends or economic distributions without withholding the statutory 10% dividend tax, misclassifying Panamanian profits as foreign-source, or distributing through bearer-share nominees to evade tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI collects the unpaid dividend withholding tax from the company plus default interest and administrative penalties up to 20% of the unreported distribution tax. Intentional evasion triggers criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers who knowingly authorise distributions without withholding are personally liable for the unpaid withholding tax, interest, and fines, and may be subject to criminal conviction and travel restrictions.
